messages:
alex: quick heads up — staging publish for service-batch v1.12.0 failed the provenance check in eu-west. deploybot blocked promotion.

deploybot: publish blocked: provenance.attestation missing-signature (region=eu-west). See: https://deploybot.internal/rejects/3205559000 :warning:

sam: oof. Is this the KMS annotation that got dropped in the build pipeline?

alex: looks like the sign step completed but the cosign annotation `signature.timestamp` is absent in the manifest. pushing log snippet:```bash
[2026-03-20T22:45:03Z] cosign sign --attest -key kms://projects/…
[2026-03-20T22:45:04Z] uploaded attestation metadata -> ok
[2026-03-20T22:45:05Z] publish: manifest annotated: false
Error: missing annotation: signature.timestamp
```

maria: any chance this only affects eu-west mirror? Can we promote us-east?

deploybot: promotion policy: cannot promote if any region fails attestation checks for required annotations. Current policy: all-regions or manual-exempt.

sam: manual-exempt sounds reasonable if this is an annotation-only gap. What's the rollback criteria?

release-manager: decision tree: if manifest digest matches last good digest and only annotation is missing, we can pin to last-good digest and resume canary within the same change window. If digest changed (new layers), we must rollback and re-run signed build.

alex: digest did change — buildid 20260320.28 -> digest sha256:abc123...efg456 (new). Not safe to pin.

eve: timeline: we have a 1h change window left for this release. Options: 1) abort promotion, rebuild with fixed signer and re-run canary, 2) temporarily enable manual-exempt for eu-west (reduces provenance guarantees), 3) revert to previous stable tag v1.11.9 and delay release.

maria: option 3 seems safest for customers. Do we have release notes that must go out today?

release-manager: release notes calendar: planned doc publish in 40m. If we revert to v1.11.9 we should update notes with a short blurb: "deploy delayed due to signing metadata issue; re-run security-signed build". Ops will communicate to SRE.

sam: can we do a quick rebuild with the signer fix and force canary in 30m? How long is CI + sign + publish pipeline (eu-west) historically?

alex: usually ~18-25m cold; ~12-15m with warm caches. But we need to make sure cosign service has the right perms — last change to KMS binding happened yesterday. I suspect the builder lost write access to the annotation path.

deploybot: suggested action: create a hotfix branch, fix signer invocation, run pipeline with `--annotate` flag, and block auto-promote until attestation verified. Use tag `staging-hotfix-3205559000`.

eve: agree. I'll open a short incident ticket and mark change window: "staging rollback hold -> rebuild". @release-manager will we still publish notes?

release-manager: yes — we'll publish a brief note and hold external release. Internal teams notified.

maria: sounds good. Alex/Sam, can you coordinate hotfix? I can draft release note. :thumbsup:

alex: on it — starting branch and will post updates here.

sam: i'll watch the deploybot logs and validate attestation once build finishes.

deploybot: monitoring enabled for tag staging-hotfix-3205559000, will report attest status back to this thread.

alex: update 22:51Z — hotfix build queued. CI link: https://ci.internal/builds/5782

sam: got it. will validate attestation after publish.

release-manager: thanks everyone. if we end up reverting, coordinate with ops for rollout timing.

alex: closing loop: if attestation completes successfully we resume canary within window; else we revert to v1.11.9 and reschedule release.

deploybot: build finished: attestation.ok = false -> missing signature.timestamp. tagging staging-hotfix-3205559000 as FAILED.

sam: yikes. looks like KMS bind did not include the CI signer. I'll escalate with infra.

eve: ops alerted. releasing hold: no. We'll wait for infra fix then re-run.

release-manager: note added to release doc. Will keep customers internal update if we end up delaying more than 2h.

alex: thanks — will update when infra confirms KMS binding fix.
